channel.description: 每6小时更新，推荐 alphaxiv 上最近30天 cs.IR 热门论文

item.title: From Head to Tail: LLM-Augmented Sequential Recommendation and Trade-off Optimization
item.description: Recommender systems exhibit popularity bias, often under-serving long-tail and cold-start items with sparse interaction data. We propose a group-specific data augmentation approach that leverages LLMs to generate synthetic interactions, formulated as a constrained optimization problem, maximizing group-specific NDCG@20 and coverage while bounding overall NDCG@20 degradation within an acceptable threshold. Items are partitioned by interaction frequency to find the optimal augmentation strategy fo...

item.title: Ask Again: Answer-List Instability in Generative Engines
item.description: Visibility in generative search engines is measured by which entities appear in responses, and in what order. Ask an engine the same question twice and the answer list can change: a different ordering, or different items altogether. Across 60,000 responses, we find that answers to the same prompt name a different first item 32% of the time, and even two answers with the same items disagree on which comes first. The first position is a measurement target of its own. A "clear leader" emerges after...

item.title: CO-GRAFT: Attributing Reinforcement Learning Gains in Search Agents via Role-Level Policy Grafting
item.description: Reinforcement learning (RL) improves large language model search agents by up to 32 exact-match (EM) points over their pre-RL initializations, yet overall accuracy gains do not identify which underlying functional capabilities improve or interact during training. We introduce CO-GRAFT, a reward-agnostic interventional attribution framework in which an RL-trained agent and its pre-RL initialization jointly generate a single trajectory under closed-loop execution with live retrieval. Each policy c...

item.title: Orthogonally Mixed Sign Coding with Progressive Residual Refinement for Transformer Weight Compression
item.description: LLM quantization reduces storage but often degrades predictive fidelity at low bit rates. We propose a training-free, CDF-free, Gaussian-CLT-motivated progressive residual-sign quantization framework that uses randomized orthogonal mixing to promote Gaussian-like residual distributions and improve sign based reconstruction of Transformer weights. Each stage independently normalizes residuals and analytically calibrates reconstruction, progressively recovering quantization errors. The framework e...

item.title: Trallie: from Free-Form Text to Structured Data with LLMs
item.description: Trallie is an open-source framework that leverages large language models (LLMs) to perform information extraction (IE) from natural language sources with or without user guidance. Unlike conventional approaches that rely on extensive labeled datasets or domain-specific training, Trallie enables the conversion of unstructured data into structured formats with minimal or no representative examples. The framework is designed with three key objectives: (i) reducing manual annotation by harnessing pr...

item.title: Beyond Knowledge Transfer: How User Overlap Shapes Diversity in Cross-Domain Recommendation
item.description: A common paradigm in cross-domain recommendation (CDR) transfers knowledge through users shared by source and target domains. Although this overlap bridge is effective in improving accuracy, its effect on diversity remains unclear. We identify two bottlenecks: the bridge can be too narrow when overlapping users cover limited target-domain tastes, and too loud when shared signals dominate the sparse personal evidence of non-overlapping users. To address both, we propose DivCDR, a model-agnostic P...

item.title: SuSi-RAG: A Hybrid Graph RAG for Equipment Maintenance
item.description: In the manufacturing domain, equipment maintenance tasks depend on expert knowledge. Their documentation is often stored in heterogeneous formats and sources. The enhancement of LLMs with Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) is promising for bridging the scattered knowledge, but traditional vector-based RAG shows weaknesses with two characteristics which are common in real maintenance queries: complex causal chains and cross-domain synthesis. To address this, we propose SuSi-RAG, a hybrid Graph ...

item.title: Fetch, Read, Reuse: How AI Search Agents Bend the Web's Rules
item.description: AI search agents form a new and fast-growing class of web traffic. Like a browser, they fetch pages on demand for one user; like a transcoding proxy, they rewrite what they fetch; and like a shared cache, they answer other users' questions from the stored copy. The rules publishers rely on, such as http://robots.txt, Retry-After, and Cache-Control, were written for more familiar clients, so the agent's vendor decides which of them to follow. We present a black-box measurement study of how these ...

item.title: PROSPER: LLMs as Sparse Retrievers for First-Stage Product Search
item.description: Product search is a crucial component of large-scale e-commerce platforms, where first-stage retrieval should achieve high recall while ensuring efficient online deployment. Sparse retrieval remains attractive for this setting due to its interpretability and deployability, yet it suffers from severe vocabulary mismatch challenges, especially for short queries and product titles. Large language models (LLMs) offer strong semantic capabilities, but directly applying them to sparse retrieval in pro...

item.title: Can Search Agents Correct Their Own Errors? Evaluating Retrieval, Evidence Delivery, and Answer Completion
item.description: A search agent can leave an earlier error unresolved by missing the right source, overlooking a relevant passage, or failing to revise and deliver the answer after receiving the evidence. We evaluate these possibilities on BrowseComp-Plus by replaying each model's own wrong closed-book answer in conversation and intervening on what evidence reaches the model. In a supplied-evidence study spanning four open-weight checkpoints, 709 questions and 26,665 test conditions, a confident assistant prior ...

item.title: Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields with Bidirectional Diffusion Encoders for Zero-Training Cross-Ontology Medical Coding
item.description: Healthcare systems continually revise clinical taxonomies, update reimbursement schedules, and harmonize cross-border registries. Existing automated coding models bind clinical text understanding to fixed vocabulary-specific heads, requiring manual relabeling and retraining whenever code sets change. We introduce Ontology-Compiled 2D Clinical State Fields (OCSF), a vocabulary-free framework that decouples clinical document reading from target ontology indexing so one trained encoder can switch a...

item.title: Weight Coding: Evolving Web-Scale Recommenders through Direct Weight Edits with LLM Agents
item.description: Web-scale recommender models evolve primarily through retraining or fine-tuning. We propose \emph{weight coding}, a methodology for model evolution through direct, executable weight edits. A large language model (LLM) agent inspects model structure and parameters, formulates hypotheses, and implements edits using evaluation feedback. The loop progresses from localized changes to targeted searches and composition, allowing edited components to adapt to one another. A cached engine enables rapid f...

item.title: Pixel as the Common Language: Unified Multimodal Embedding via Visual Rendering
item.description: Multimodal embedding models map heterogeneous inputs into a shared representation space, yet text-only, image-only, and composed inputs are still presented in distinct formats and follow different routes through the model. This fragmentation prevents heterogeneous tasks from jointly optimizing the same end-to-end encoding process, limiting supervision transfer across input configurations. To address this issue, we propose unification before encoding and instantiate this paradigm in RenderEmbed. ...

item.title: STUN-Bench: Truly Unseen Tools for Evaluating Shared Tool Experience
item.description: A tool router retrieves a few candidate tools per request and lets a language model choose. Methods that share experience across organizations add past requests about each tool to what the router retrieves. StableToolBench calls some of its test groups tests on "unseen" tools, yet the ToolBench instruction pool, which retrievers and experience-sharing methods learn from, contains every test query and labels every gold tool of the two single-tool groups among them. We release STUN-Bench (StableTo...

item.title: SHAKTI: Evidence-Grounded Conversational AI for Nutrition and Health
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) answer many diet and health questions but can state unsupported claims and cite sources that do not support them. We present SHAKTI (Smart Health Advisor for Knowledge-based Tailored Interventions), a conversational assistant that answers only from retrieved scholarly papers and exact food-composition data, and evaluate it with retrieval, generation, grounding, efficiency and contextawareness metrics. We indexed 484,368,086 OpenAlex works, searched exactly on a GPU f...

item.title: Structure-Exploiting Hierarchical Retrieval for Long Narrative Documents: A Precision-Oriented Alternative to Learned Abstraction Trees
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation over book-length documents must locate a small, coherent set of passages inside tens of thousands of tokens. Flat dense retrieval ignores document structure; RAPTOR instead builds a hierarchy by recursively clustering and summarizing with a language model. We study a complementary design that exploits the native structure of a document: a two-level retriever that (i) selects chapters with a hybrid BM25+dense match over chapter recaps, (ii) runs a chapter-filtered d...

item.title: Look Before You Leap: Re-Architecting Disk-Resident Vector Search with TriVS
item.description: Disk-resident approximate nearest-neighbor search (ANNS) scales vector search beyond DRAM, yet state-of-the-art systems remain I/O-bound, even with fast SSDs and sophisticated I/O execution. To understand this bottleneck, we conduct an I/O-centric analysis that breaks each query down into an approach phase that locates a query-near region and a converge phase that resolves the final top-k. This analysis reveals complementary I/O tradeoffs: cluster-based search circumvents approach-phase I/O thro...

item.title: Bridging Blind Spots With Words: Decentralized Multi-View Spatial Reasoning via Language-Constrained Communication
item.description: As multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) get increasingly used as collaborative partners across embodied robotics, AR/VR, and multi-user systems, spatial reasoning is now often distributed across agents with partial environment visibility, necessitating spatial reasoning integration. Prior work in language-mediated spatial integration is however strictly limited to simplified two-agent scenarios. To address this gap, we first formalize the general problem of decentralized multi-view spatial reasoning, where N...

item.title: Where Do Fact-Checking Errors Arise? Separating Retrieval, Search Control and Judgement in Evidence-Grounded Verification
item.description: An evidence-grounded fact-checker can fail because it does not find the evidence or because it does not use it; end-to-end accuracy does not tell the two apart. We present a protocol that follows the reference evidence from the store to the verdict and separates retrieval, search control, judgement and verdict validation. We assess 293 claims from FEVER, FEVER 2.0 and AVeriTeC with one open-weights 9B model under two evidence conditions: small stores of annotated evidence, where discovery is eas...

item.title: MoR4Rec: Mixture-of-Recursion for Sequential Recommendation
item.description: Sequential recommender systems aim to predict a user's next interaction by modeling temporal dependencies in historical behavior sequences. To capture such dependencies, recent approaches increasingly rely on attention-based architectures, particularly transformers. While effective at modeling long-range sequential patterns, these models apply a fixed computation depth to all interaction items, treating them as equally complex. However, user behavior is inherently heterogeneous, with many intera...

item.title: VistaTree: Question Answering over Long Multimodal Documents with Image-Derived Summary Trees
item.description: Answering questions over long multimodal documents requires locating relevant evidence across pages containing text, tables, and figures. When the document exceeds the model's context window, selective retrieval becomes necessary. We introduce VistaTree, a document question-answering agent that builds a summary tree directly from rendered page images. VistaTree segments documents into contiguous page spans, recursively groups them into a topic hierarchy, and refines sibling summaries to distingu...

item.title: LLM-Based Assistant for Dog Care Guidance
item.description: This study investigates whether domain grounding through Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) and parameter-efficient fine-tuning using Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) can enhance the accuracy and reliability of pet care advice generated by large language models (LLMs). We curated a dataset of breed-specific dog care information and used it to develop two systems: a RAG pipeline based on TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0, and a fine-tuned LLaMA-3.2-1B model adapted using LoRA. Both systems were evaluated on 1...

item.title: NoeVera: Can Knowledge Guide Experiments and Experiments Refine Knowledge?
item.description: With the growing demand for large language model (LLM) services, optimizing LLM serving systems is becoming increasingly complex, and the bottleneck is no longer predicting how a given configuration will perform. The harder problem is deciding what to investigate: which mechanisms matter for a workload, which configurations are worth testing, and what evidence a decision still needs. In this work, we present NoeVera, an agentic Second Brain that goes beyond just one-shot retrieval by turning pap...

item.title: Zarc: Exact Nearest Neighbors over a Billion Vectors in Seconds
item.description: Exact k-nearest-neighbor vector search lies on the critical path of machine learning systems, from sparse attention in the latest large language models (LLMs) to long-context memories and training-data deduplication. Exhaustive GPU search scans the whole dataset for every query, while approximate indexes return inexact neighbors. Recent methods skip almost every vector with a cheap half-precision proof that it lies too far away, but only on one GPU that holds the whole dataset. Our insight is to...

item.title: DataRecycle: Trustworthy Distillation of Structured Data from Scattered Web Evidence
item.description: The web contains vast amounts of scattered quantitative evidence that is difficult to organize into comparable and verifiable structures. Yet its unstructured, sparse, and sometimes conflicting nature makes a systematic distillation costly and error-prone. Existing approaches force users to make a trade-off: search engines return document lists that require labor-intensive extraction and reconciliation, while generative AI systems produce fluent summaries that obscure data provenance, introduce ...

item.title: HME-PFD: Heterogeneous Mixture-of-Experts Privileged Feature Distillation
item.description: Knowledge distillation (KD) is widely used to transfer knowledge from large teacher models to smaller student models, facilitating efficient serving of machine learning systems. In the context of ads recommendation, privileged features distillation (PFD) extends KD by allowing the teacher model to leverage privileged features, i.e., features available only during training, to enhance distillation performance. However, in real-world scenarios, privileged features often have limited coverage and e...

item.title: Who Gets Re-ranked When a Clinical Model Gains New Data?
item.description: Hospitals often update a deployed risk model by adding a data source, such as laboratory results, that only some patients have. Work on safe model updates assumes fixed inputs and so ignores patients who lack the new data. The update has no new measurements for them, yet their rank can change, and a sick patient not yet tested can drop off an alert list. We split rank-based compatibility by data availability and pair it with error correction and alert-list effects. We compared each update with o...

item.title: ChatGPT Can't Sell (And That's Probably a Good Thing): Buyer-Aligned AI Advice, the Sales-Representative Gap, and Evidence from Commercial Conversations
item.description: AI assistants and merchant sales agents have different objectives: assistants should help buyers compare options and preserve the choice not to purchase, while sales agents also guide qualified buyers toward an authorized next step. We study this sales-representative gap with three evidence streams. In 12,178 historical English GPT-family conversations screened for commercial or transactional intent, a 279-request sample contained recommendation language in 63 first replies (22.6%) and no narrow...

item.title: MADRec: Reliable Multi-Agent Reasoning with Evidence-Grounded Debate for Recommendation
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) are transforming recommender systems from conventional preference matching toward reasoning-driven and explainable decision-making. Multi-agent collaboration further advances this paradigm by distributing recommendation reasoning across specialized agents. However, existing frameworks rarely assess the reliability of intermediate reasoning during collaboration, allowing erroneous judgments to propagate across agents and ultimately degrade recommendation quality. To a...

item.title: The abc index: Exact Retrieval for Learned Sparse Representations
item.description: In learned sparse retrieval (LSR), queries have tens of terms with learned weights, on which classic dynamic pruning is believed to fail, and approximate indexes such as Seismic and HNSW are considered faster than exact ones. We challenge this view with abc, an exact index built only from standard IR techniques: term-at-a-time (TAAT) evaluation, Block-Max MaxScore, binary packing and doc-id reordering. They are combined in a new design and engineered for modern CPUs. On MS MARCO encoded with fou...

item.title: Beyond Relevance: An Empirical Study of Multimodal LLMs for Diversity-Aware Recommendation Reranking
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) have emerged as promising rerankers for recommendation, yet most existing approaches rely on textual item descriptions and primarily focus on relevance. In visually oriented domains such as video streaming, item images provide complementary signals that may also inform recommendation diversity. This raises two questions: when does visual information improve recommendation quality, and can multimodal LLMs (MLLMs) enhance relevance and diversity simultaneously? We inve...

item.title: GERF: A Token-Efficient Multimodal Retrieval Framework for Schema-Guided Scientific Information Extraction
item.description: Scientific information extraction (IE) is a fundamental component of AI for Science, transforming experimental knowledge embedded in scientific literature into structured and traceable data for evidence synthesis, scientific database construction, and data-driven discovery. However, critical experimental details are often distributed across text, tables, figures, captions, and surrounding discussion, making them difficult to recover using conventional text-only extraction. Existing LLM-based and...

item.title: DM-Lab at TREC 2026 RAG: Multi-Query Retrieval, Ensemble Judging, and Claim-Pack Generation
item.description: We present DM-Lab-RAG-2026, a framework developed for the TREC 2026 Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) track. The framework integrates large-scale evidence retrieval and citation-grounded answer generation over the 553-million-document ClimbMix-400B corpus. The retrieval architecture combines multi-query BM25, reciprocal rank fusion, ensemble relevance assessment, listwise reranking, and adaptive retrieval depth. The generation pipeline employs a claim-first strategy to extract evidence-linked...

item.title: Evaluating Memanto on DolphinBench for AI Agents
item.description: Memory benchmarks built on question answering tell an agent which fact to recall. Workplace requests often leave that need implicit: to post an update in the team's channel, an agent must work out which channel from earlier interactions and use it in a tool call. We evaluate Memanto, a memory agent that ranks memories with an information-theoretic relevance score, on DolphinBench, which tests memory through 600 simulated workplace tasks, each validated as requiring memory. Running in the Hermes ...

item.title: Close the Loop on the Retrievability Gap
item.description: A frozen vision-language encoder now guides image restoration and later indexes what it produced. Over a fixed set of eighteen pansharpening systems on one WorldView-III test set, the fidelity index that ranks them, $Q2^n$ with a reference and HQNR without one, picks the less retrievable of two systems one time in three and one in two; the disagreement lies between the pixel-supervised and the language-conditioned family, and even the best system falls short of the reference, small objects first...

item.title: Which Dwarf Is This? Doppeldwarf-306 and Near-Identical Instance Retrieval
item.description: Most established instance-retrieval benchmarks emphasise landmarks; small sculptures from visually similar series offer a complementary challenge. We introduce Doppeldwarf-306: 1,691 openly licensed photographs of 306 bronze dwarf statues in Wrocław, Poland, many made in themed series that share one style, with the photographer of each image recorded. With no training, nearest-neighbour search over frozen DINOv2 features names the right statue first for 93.1% of leave-one-out queries, and the be...

item.title: Deep Cross-Division Network for Product-and-Ratio Feature Interactions in Industrial Ranking
item.description: Learning effective feature interactions is essential for industrial recommender systems. DCN and DCNv2 efficiently automate polynomial feature crossing. However, their cross layers construct interactions using only non-negative integer powers of the input features, with the maximum degree controlled by network depth. Consequently, they cannot directly represent the reciprocal terms required for ratios, rates, and normalized counts unless such features are explicitly provided as inputs. We introd...

item.title: DiTraR: Diverse Scorers and Transcript-Guided Re-ranking for Video Corpus Moment Retrieval
item.description: Video corpus moment retrieval asks a system to find, in a large collection of untrimmed videos with subtitles, the video and the time interval that a natural-language query describes. We find that most top-ranked errors of a strong corpus-level scorer come from choosing the wrong video, not from imprecise boundaries, and that re-weighting the evidence the scorer already uses does not fix them. We present DiTraR, which addresses video selection from two complementary directions. A witness-interva...

item.title: Decision Columns as an Index: Interpretable Embeddings for Explainable Entity Matching and Search
item.description: Business data systems must determine whether records refer to the same entity and retrieve records satisfying requests whose decisive properties are implicit. As agents act on these records, both tasks require auditable reasons. Dense embeddings perform well but offer opaque coordinates, cannot be filtered by meaning, and require corpus re-encoding to add new properties. We propose interpretable embeddings built from decision columns: each column stores a decision model&apos;s calibrated answer to a ...

item.title: Explicit Style Extraction for Personalized Long-Form Text Generation
item.description: Personalized long-form generation asks a language model to write new text the way a specific user would. The standard recipe, retrieval-augmented generation, places a few of the user&apos;s past texts in the prompt but leaves the model to decide what to take from them. We introduce StylePrism, a taxonomy of 28 stylistic aspects in seven categories, and SP-Refine, an inference-time method that makes style extraction an explicit step: the model first fills StylePrism with the user&apos;s patterns, quoted ev...

item.title: Pre-Crawl Prioritization and Seed Classification for Large-Scale Web Archiving
item.description: Pre-crawl prioritization systems decide which pages to fetch first before indexing, aiming to improve crawl efficiency and coverage. Existing approaches based on page popularity and relevance are unsuited to web-archival crawlers that prioritize comprehensive coverage over selective retrieval. We explore prioritization techniques tailored to web archival operations using URL lexical analysis, dynamic domain reputation systems, and HTTP response analysis to inform crawl scheduling decisions. By i...

item.title: ERA: Embed, Route, Adapt for Cold-Start Cross-Model Latent Retrieval
item.description: Production retrieval systems are tied to the embedding model that indexed their corpus. Moving queries to a different encoder normally requires re-embedding the whole corpus, and at cold start there are no query logs while every document embedded by the new encoder incurs an API or compute cost. We present ERA (Embed, Route, Adapt), a system for cold-start cross-model latent retrieval. ERA spends a small anchor budget on maximally informative documents, selected from the existing target index vi...

item.title: Leader Finding: A New Variation of Expert Finding in Community Question Answering
item.description: Expert finding ranks people by their knowledge of a given topic. Many job positions need more than topical expertise, and a team leader is a clear case. A suitable leader knows the technical areas of the project without being overqualified, has strong managerial knowledge, and communicates well with the team. We study the leader finding problem, where the query is a project and a team and the output is a ranked list of candidate leaders. We model the problem in a probabilistic framework that com...

item.title: DNA: Unlocking Depth Scaling in CTR Models
item.description: Long user behavior sequences are among the strongest signals for click-through rate (CTR) prediction. Cross-attention makes these sequences practical for industrial ranking by keeping compute linear in sequence length. Yet the gains from stacking cross-attention layers taper off: on Taobao search, growing a cross-attention stack from 16 to 28 layers adds only 0.02 percentage points (pt) of AUC. We argue that the key-value side is the bottleneck. Each layer projects the same behavior sequence int...

item.title: LQ-Rec: Late Quantization for Sequential Recommendation
item.description: Generative retrieval (GR) for sequential recommendation compresses each item into a short semantic ID and trains an autoregressive decoder to generate next-item codes from a user history. While appealing for cold-start handling and storage, au- toregressive GR suffers a structural scaling limit: typically, longer semantic IDs reduce quantization error in principle but degrade ranking quality and quadratic memory usage against semantic ID length. We propose Late Quantization (LQ), a non-autoregre...

item.title: LINEAGE: A Benchmark for Empirical Lineage Retrieval in AI Scientific Literature
item.description: Current research agents are moving beyond academic search toward literature synthesis and experiment planning. These workflows increasingly rely on literature retrieval systems, which serve as standalone systems or as components of research agents. However, existing scientific literature retrieval benchmarks mainly evaluate these methods using topical relevance or citation links as supervision, which cannot capture which prior methods are used for empirical comparison. To address this gap, we in...

item.title: AutoRAGBench: A Benchmark for LLM Agents Automating RAG System Development
item.description: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) is a well-established paradigm for augmenting large language models (LLMs) with information retrieved from external corpora. However, developing effective RAG systems requires substantial engineering effort and iterative experimentation, as effective design choices vary across tasks and domains. With rapid advances in LLM agent capabilities, we ask how well these agents can autonomously build RAG systems and how effectively they can improve them through itera...

item.title: LSP-RAG: Latent Scoring Perspectives for Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation
item.description: Large Language Models (LLMs) have demonstrated strong capabilities in open-domain question answering, but often struggle with factual accuracy and multi-hop reasoning due to the incompleteness of the training corpora. A promising solution is Knowledge Graph Retrieval-Augmented Generation (KG-RAG), which supplements LLMs with structured knowledge retrieved from external knowledge graphs (KGs). However, existing KG-RAG methods either rely on large-scale language models (e.g., ChatGPT) to guide the...

item.title: Cost-Aware Agentic Feature Optimization System for Fleet-Scale Ranking Models
item.description: Large Web platforms operate large fleets of ranking models, each selecting features from a shared pool of tens of thousands. We present an end-to-end agentic system that optimizes features across the fleet under resource constraints shared across models and those set per model, such as feature pipeline cost and serving throughput (QPS), respectively. In this system, LLM agents propose hypotheses, and deterministic tools execute experiments and verify them. For each model, an LLM generates and sh...

item.title: From Sessions to Serving: Integrating LLM-Based Embeddings into Retrieval for Production Content Recommendation
item.description: Personalized content recommendation on large marketplace websites must reconcile heterogeneous candidate content (e.g., customer stories, product pages, industry pages, and learning content) with sparse, fast-changing user behavior, placing increasing demands on the retrieval stage to represent user interest well, not just the downstream ranking stage. We present LSER (LLM Session Embedding Retrieval), a production content recommendation system for http://autodesk.com that derives session- and h...

item.title: CACO: Coverage-Aware Coordinated Optimization for Continuous Generative Retrieval
item.description: Continuous generative retrievers powered by flow matching and diffusion sample multiple queries in item embedding space for parallel approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search under fixed retrieval budgets. However, optimizing distribution diversity or target-level interest separation ignores set-level retrieval geometry: sampled queries collapse onto overlapping ANN neighborhoods, while discrete top-K lookup and single-target supervision block end-to-end coverage optimization. We introduce CACO ...

item.title: Variants of Beam Search for DiskANN
item.description: Graph-based data structures such as DiskANN, HNSW, and NSG constitute the state of the art for large-scale approximate nearest-neighbor (ANN) search. Indyk and Xu introduced the notion of $\alpha$-reachable graphs, which include graphs built by DiskANN&amp;apos;s slow-preprocessing construction, and proved that greedy search achieves an approximation factor of $\tfrac{\alpha+1}{\alpha-1}$. Independently, Al-Jazzazi et al. proposed adaptive beam search (ABS) with a relaxation parameter $\gamma &amp;amp;gt; 0$, sh...

item.title: FinVeriQA: Financial Research Agents for Question Answering: Routing, Retrieval, MCP Tool Use, and Provenance-Aware Evidence Verification
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) write fluent financial analyses but miscompute ratios, recall stale prices, and route questions to the wrong tool with high confidence. We ask which component should do each job in a financial question-answering assistant, and study it with FinVeriQA, an open-source multi-agent research prototype over SEC filings and live market data: a compact typed-decision model (Laya) routes each question and screens out advice requests, Python computes every number, retrieval an...

item.title: The Window Lever: Longer Observation Windows Outweigh the Observed Effects of Data, Capacity, and Architecture in Customer Behavior Forecasting
item.description: In our experiments on long-horizon customer-behavior forecasting, a longer observation window outweighed the observed effects of more data, more capacity and newer architectures. The window is the weeks of history a model sees before the week it forecasts from. Going from an 8- to a 16-week window adds a raw +0.070 to 0.107 log-space $R^2$ in every family at 1M. Matched test cohorts, which score the same customer-weeks at every window, show this raw comparison understates the gain in every famil...

item.title: Democratizing Cross-Project Knowledge for Transforming Water Governance and Climate Resilience: an Agentic AI Ecosystem
item.description: EU-funded projects produce extensive evidence in the form of deliverables, reports, and case studies. However, this knowledge is typically scattered across projects and document structures, making it difficult to locate relevant, contextual information when making decisions. This paper introduces an Agentic AI Ecosystem that consolidates heterogeneous project documentation into a domain-aware knowledge base and provides adaptive access through an agentic Retrieval-Augmented Generation pipeline. ...

item.title: VideoTrail: Interactive Video Foraging Through Hierarchical Visualization
item.description: People often watch videos to find information, but locating relevant moments can be difficult and time-consuming. Existing strategies like scrubbing rely primarily on visual scanning and linear search, providing limited support for goal-directed navigation. We present VideoTrail, an AI-powered browser extension that supports information seeking in videos through a hierarchical visualization. Inspired by information foraging theory, VideoTrail surfaces semantic and structural cues as information ...

item.title: A Task-Level Bias Taxonomy for Historical Image Retrieval
item.description: In recent decades, galleries, libraries, archives, and museums (GLAM institutions) have digitised vast amounts of cultural heritage material, including historical imagery. A major challenge in making these collections publicly accessible is enabling effective search and discovery. Many historical images contain incomplete, sparse, or no descriptive metadata. Consequently, machine learning (ML) methods are increasingly being used to generate or enrich metadata to improve the searchability of such...

item.title: Can LLMs Resolve Entity Conflicts in Domain Specific NLU Pipelines?
item.description: Resolving entity conflicts is a critical step in Pipeline-based NLU architectures, especially when multiple extractors provide overlapping or conflicting outputs. Traditional rule-based entity conflict resolution methods often lack flexibility and are unscalable. In this work, we aim to study if the broad knowledge of LLMs can be leveraged to resolve entity conflicts in domain specific NLU pipelines. We present an experimental comparison between a traditional rule-based conflict resolution metho...

item.title: STARK: Moving towards Personalized Agents That Truly Learn and Remember
item.description: Long-term memory is essential for personalized agentic systems that interact with users over long time periods, yet current architectures only capture what happened while leaving the reasoning of why it happened to be derived later by underlying LLMs.%, and silo knowledge within individual users. These events can, however, convey not only what a user experienced but also how that experience shaped their behavioral patterns. We introduce STARK, a dual-graph memory architecture which treats these ...

item.title: Exploring Semantic Table Search in Data Lakes
item.description: Discovery of relevant datasets within data lakes remains a key challenge. Union and join search are effective techniques for discovering data when augmenting an existing table. In exploratory search, instead, keyword search is commonly adopted to find a relatively small set of highly relevant tables matching some search terms. In this context, semantic search is a new technique that exploits the presence of named entities in exemplar tuples used as queries and in target tables. Hence, keyword se...

item.title: Uncontrolled source titles: When Nature, Science, and PNAS meet Scopus
item.description: Bibliographic databases such as Scopus and Web of Science play a critical role in literature discovery, systematic reviews, bibliometric analyses, and research evaluation, yet their reliability depends on effective control of the quality of the bibliographic data. This study examines the problem of uncontrolled source titles in Scopus by comparing five possibly adopted journal-level retrieval strategies across three flagship journals-Nature, Science, and PNAS. Substantial discrepancies across re...

item.title: Generative News Recommendation Reproduces Popularity: A Memorization-Based Analysis
item.description: Text-based generative recommenders can go beyond ranking existing items by directly generating item titles or other textual representations. In the news domain, this raises a societal concern that models may repeatedly surface already popular articles and thereby narrow the diversity of information to which users are exposed. item.title: Learning Generative Ranking Policies for Whole-Page Optimization
item.description: A recommendation page is consumed as a whole: the items on it compete for attention and complement one another, so the best page is not simply the individually best items placed side by side. We study whole-page optimization, which selects and orders the items on a page jointly to maximize the score of the page. item.title: Retrieving Patristic References and Modelling Topics in Bullinger's Reformation Correspondence
item.description: The correspondence of Heinrich Bullinger (1504-1575), Swiss Reformer and Antistes of Zurich, documents the political and religious debates of the Reformation, including extensive appeals to the Church Fathers as authoritative sources. Detecting such references computationally remains largely unexplored. item.title: MARS Technical Report
item.description: Modern industrial recommender systems use multi-stage cascades--retrieval, pre-ranking, ranking, and re-ranking--to narrow millions of candidates to a personalized list. While each stage deploys sophisticated models, pipeline-level decisions on channel activation, quotas, model selection, and score fusion remain engineer-tuned and user-agnostic within each scenario. This report presents MARS (Multi-stage Agentic Recommendation System), extending personalization from individual-stage predictions ...

item.title: Can Programs Replace LLM Judges? Executable Program Judges for Scalable and Efficient Relevance Labeling
item.description: Large language model (LLM) judges have become a common way to create large-scale relevance judgments for retrieval evaluation. However, each judgment requires a potentially expensive call to a frontier model, and the judgments are hard to interpret and may not be reproducible. In this paper, we ask whether an LLM can write a readable program for each topic that replaces its per-document judgments. item.title: KnowMe Paper Radar: Lightweight Discovery of Promising Papers in the Age of Autoresearch
item.description: The growing volume of topically similar papers makes it difficult to identify new work that can offer useful research insights or methodological guidance. We present KnowMe Paper Radar, a lightweight discovery tool that combines multiple sources of evidence into personalized reading priorities. Users specify topics, priorities, exclusions and dates; the system brings together topical relevance, recency, author research histories, collaboration paths and direction-specific institutional context. ...

item.title: X-split Argus: Learning Reusable History Tokens for Efficient CTR Prediction
item.description: Accurate click-through rate (CTR) prediction depends on user representations that capture both persistent preferences and recent intent, yet processing extensive behavioral histories for every ranking request is costly under production compute and latency constraints. We present X-split ARGUS, a framework for ad ranking whose history compressor and online ranker are trained end to end. item.title: ReflectRec: Cycle-Consistency Preference Verification for LLM-based Recommendation
item.description: CoT-style LLM recommenders generate a natural-language preference note as a chain-of-thought prefix to ranking, but the note is trusted without verification, and the ranker never consults behaviorally similar users. item.title: Variance-Optimal Counterfactual Policy Design for Sample-Efficient Online A/B Testing
item.description: Online A/B testing is the standard approach for evaluating changes to user-facing systems, such as a new recommendation or ranking policy, before deployment. While the difference-in-means estimator of a standard A/B test is unbiased, it often suffers from high variance. item.title: Task-Oriented Network Ranging via Joint Graph and Schedule Design
item.description: Measuring inter-node distances is the basis for network localization, whereas acquiring node positions does not require a fully connected graph of distances. Existing complete-ranging protocols for network localization require every node pair to exchange signals, which prolongs the ranging cycle. In this paper, we propose sparse signal-multiplexing network ranging (S-SM-NR), a task-oriented framework that adapts the transmit-listen schedule to the ranging task required by network localization. item.title: VIBRA: Backward-Compatible Cross-Modal Retrieval with Consensus Barycenters
item.description: Backward-compatible retrieval enables a new encoder to query the gallery that an old model has already encoded, so that a cross-modal retrieval system can be upgraded without re-encoding billions of items. Existing compatible methods either fit the old query and stay near the accuracy of the old model, or run the old and the new encoder for every query. item.title: CONCORD-Rec: Catalog-Conditioned Modality Utility for Semantic-ID Diffusion Recommendation
item.description: Multimodal generative recommendation with discrete semantic identifiers (SIDs) requires distinguishing historical modalities that merely alter token predictions from those that genuinely reduce catalog-level ambiguity. When audiovisual, visual, or textual streams are missing, degraded, or semantically conflicting, uniform fusion and unconstrained token gates can propagate misleading content across iterative denoising steps. item.title: From Docket Minutes to Case Trajectories: Building Analysis-Ready Criminal Court Data
item.description: Criminal court records are often fragmented, noisy, and siloed, making it challenging for both legal experts and community stakeholders to access and analyze court data to identify trends and provide public oversight. In this paper, we introduce a system for data ingestion, harmonization, and dashboard visualization designed for New Orleans criminal court proceedings data, aimed at both expert and lay audiences. item.title: LusoClin: A Synthetic Clinical Note Dataset for Medical Information Retrieval in European Portuguese
item.description: Access to large-scale clinical text collections is crucial for advancing medical information retrieval research, including clinical note search, patient cohort identification, and domain-adapted retrieval models. However, real clinical notes are rarely available due to privacy regulations, which particularly limits progress for low-resource languages such as European Portuguese. item.title: Prioritize, Don't Decide: What We Learned Auditing a Deployed Human-in-the-Loop CV Sorter
item.description: A single academic vacancy can draw hundreds of applications, and the first screening round consumes most of a committee&amp;amp;apos;s time. We describe a CV Priority Sorter deployed at a national platform for academic vacancies and integrated with its vacancy database. item.title: NONSENSE: Non-Semantic Strings Expose Semanticity Gaps in Dense Retrieval
item.description: Dense retrieval is central to modern search, question answering, and retrieval-augmented generation, where high similarity is often treated as evidence of semantic relevance. We examine how far this assumption can be stressed. NONSENSE is a black-box sparse-edit probe that constructs visibly non-semantic strings while forbidding query-term copying, optimizing only the dense similarity between a query and the string. item.title: More Than a Score: Reinforcement Learning with Verbalized Feedback for Generative Recommendation
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used for generative recommendation, where recommended items are generated directly from users&amp;amp;amp;apos; interaction histories. To further improve recommendation quality, reinforcement learning (RL) has been applied to align these models with recommendation objectives. item.title: From Relevance to Utility: Rubric Alignment in Yuanbao Search
item.description: Agentic search demands that a search engine move beyond per document relevance ranking to assemble document sets optimized for downstream LLM reasoning. Prior work addresses this either by improving individual pipeline stages in isolation or by applying RL based selection on top of relevance trained upstream modules, leaving the full stack unaligned to utility for reasoning. item.title: IntentGR: Enhancing Intent for End-to-End Personalized Generative Retrieval in Search
item.description: Personalized generative retrieval in search should jointly satisfy the user&amp;amp;amp;apos;s immediate search intent and long-term preference. item.title: MIPR: A Benchmark for Reasoning-Intensive Multimodal Intent-to-Product Retrieval with Multi-Category Solutions
item.description: Real-world e-commerce queries often express user intent without naming a target product, and a single intent may be fulfilled by products from multiple categories. item.title: CARE: Conversational Affective Response Retrieval for Internet Memes
item.description: Conversational meme retrieval supports response selection in online communication, where relevance depends on both contextual meaning and affective expression. We study this task using two language-specific collections from Douban and Imgflip, containing 98,506 meme records across 5,583 discussion topics. item.title: Learning Cross-Domain Media Similarity from Amazon Reviews
item.description: Collaborative filtering is a basic foundation of many recommendation algorithms. It works by analyzing a user&amp;amp;amp;apos;s history and then suggesting items similar to those in that history. item.title: SIMQ: A Single Graph-based Index for Multi-Vector Query
item.description: Multi-vector retrieval models such as ColBERT achieve state-of-the-art effectiveness by representing documents as sets of token-level vectors and scoring via MaxSim, but their high computational cost limits scalability to large corpora. item.title: RICoT: Recurrent Interleaved Chain-of-Thought for Page Stream Segmentation
item.description: Large language models (LLMs) have renewed interest in Page Stream Segmentation (PSS), splitting a multi-page file into its constituent documents. Yet published LLM methods still frame the task as boundary classification over one or a few neighboring pages, and commercial document-splitting APIs do not disclose their methods. item.title: Complexity and precision in quantum associative retrieval
item.description: We show that efficient and high-precision quantum associative retrieval is possible with an exponential complexity advantage with respect to the classical brute force approach and with a polynomial capacity advantage with respect to classical neural network implementations for any number of patterns scaling polynomially in the number of qubits. item.title: Teaching Language Models to Narrow Boolean Patent Searches from Search Feedback
item.description: Patent prior-art searchers issue Boolean queries line by line, broadening to find relevant documents and narrowing until candidates can be screened. We distill 38,397 Japan Patent Office search reports into executable expert strategies, re-execute them, and evaluate generated strategies by citation recall and the smallest set containing each citation. item.title: When the tail is earned by its companions: measuring label dependence in long-tailed multi-label classification
item.description: A rare label seldom occurs alone, and a classifier can recover it from the frequent labels it co-occurs with, its companions, without having learned the label itself. item.title: Music Similarity Learning in Sparse Latin Scenarios
item.description: In this work we propose a lightweight, interpretable approach that estimates item-item music similarity from publicly available metadata. Our hybrid regression model combines content-based filtering with the classic item-based collaborative filtering. item.title: Better Rankers, Worse Retrievers: The Hidden Cost of RL Post-Training in Generative Recommendation
item.description: Generative recommenders decode the semantic ID of a user&amp;amp;amp;apos;s next item with a language model, and post-training them with reinforcement learning (RL) after supervised fine-tuning (SFT) has become standard practice. item.title: Deal With It: On Better Schedules for Listwise Reranking
item.description: Listwise LLM rerankers cannot reliably rank hundreds of documents in a single call, and rely on schedules to orchestrate their calls. Parallel schedules split candidates into groups and advance a fixed quota from each. item.title: GuardAgent: A Memory-Augmented Agentic Framework for Adaptive Detection of Adversarial Promotions in LLM-Based Recommendation
item.description: In traditional recommender systems (RSs), textual information typically serves as auxiliary signals for representation learning. In contrast, in LLM-based RSs, textual information becomes the primary medium for recommendation generation through semantic understanding and reasoning. item.title: Cluster-Guided Decoding with Trust-Region Constraints for Personalized Recommendation
item.description: Most recommenders score each item in the catalog separately, and do not explicitly model which semantic region of the catalog a recommendation belongs to. Models expressive enough to offer that control are often too slow to run over a full catalog for online inference. In this paper, we present Cluster-Guided Generative Reconstruction (CG2R), which learns a hierarchy of semantic clusters and uses a cluster-level prior to steer item ranking for personalized recommendations. item.title: Beyond Bitwidth: Deployment-Constrained Mixed-Precision Quantization for Multilingual LLM Inference on NVIDIA Blackwell
item.description: Low-bit LLM quantization is useful only if a model preserves service-relevant accuracy, executes through supported GPU kernels, and meets measured memory and latency limits. item.title: Urban Representation Learning for Identifying Potential Disparities in Crime Reporting
item.description: Open crime data support urban safety analysis but reflect reported incidents rather than the complete distribution of criminal activity, potentially introducing spatial distortions in downstream analysis. We propose a self-supervised urban representation learning framework for identifying unusual reporting patterns relative to representation-similar peers using only georeferenced crime records. item.title: ExRel: Learning Directed Reuse Relevance between Rich-Text K-12 Question Images with Executable Relation Contracts
item.description: In K-12 education, question images combine text, mathematical expressions, diagrams, and diverse layouts. Variations in wording, conditions, answer options, or task scope can substantially alter their reuse utility despite visual similarity. item.title: How did data sharing evolve in the decade since the FAIR Principles?
item.description: A decade after the publication of the FAIR Guiding Principles, what have we learned about data sharing, and what do data availability statements (DAS) and other materials accrued over that period tell us about how data-sharing practices, attitudes, and infrastructures evolved? Here, we present a large-scale longitudinal analysis of over 6.8 million biomedical articles from the PMC Open Access Subset, spanning 2011 to 2025. item.title: TokenFormer V2: Breaking the Resolution-Complexity Dilemma in Unified Recommendation
item.description: Industrial recommendation faces a resolution--complexity dilemma: dense interactions make detailed modeling of long behavior histories expensive, while compact history summaries restrict the evidence available to prediction. item.title: Living Context Graphs: Continual Semantic Learning for Enterprise Data Reasoning
item.description: Enterprise AI can now perform analytics, reporting, and data-driven workflows, yet the data foundations it relies on remain hard to operationalize: business meaning, relationships, metric definitions, and reporting conventions are absent from database schemas and scattered across undocumented systems and tribal knowledge. item.description: When several candidates have graph support, does it matter which candidate receives which supporter and path counts?
